Full Text Search in MAM This specification proposes a field in the MAM form for full text searching. &LEGALNOTICE; 0431 Deferred Standards Track Standards

section1.p: &xep0313; has an extensible form. This specification extends the extensible form with an extension which extends MAM to perform full text searching. A number of existing implementations of this extension exist - extending their existing extensions to conform to the extension in this specification now it exists is intended to be trivial.

This specification defines two flavours of search that servers can offer and that clients can use. To ensure maxiumum interoperability and usability, servers SHOULD offer simple searches whenever possible, and MAY offer advanced searches.

section2.p: A simple search consists of a plain text natural-language string which is desired in the messages returned from a search query. Servers may apply various techniques appropriate for a natural-language search - such as stemming and filtering of stop words. However, the string MUST NOT be interpreted as containing any special syntax, keywords or operators, even if such syntax is supported by the server's underlying search engine.

If simple searches are supported by the server, it should include a text field in the MAM query form with the name {&ns;}fulltext#simple and advertise the urn:xmpp:fulltext:0#simple feature via Service Discovery.

Within the <field/> element, the server MAY indicate to the client a list of languages via the <lang/> element in the &ns; namespace. The text content of this element should be a comma-separated list of languages supported by the server, identified by their ISO 631-1 codes. The intent of this field is not to restrict what languages may be used with the search function, but to provide hints to the client (and user) when the search functionality is optimized for particular languages. If the server's search functionality is language-agnostic, then the <lang/> element MUST NOT be included in the field.

example.caption: Server offers simple text search functionality

section2.example: <iq type='result' id='form1'> <query xmlns='urn:xmpp:mam:2'> <x xmlns='jabber:x:data' type='form'> <field type='hidden' var='FORM_TYPE'> <value>urn:xmpp:mam:2</value> </field> <field type='jid-single' var='with'/> <field type='text-single' var='start'/> <field type='text-single' var='end'/> <field type='text-single' var='{urn:xmpp:fulltext:0}fulltext#simple'> <lang xmlns="urn:xmpp:fulltext:0">en,fr</lang> </field> </x> </query> </iq>

section2.p: An advanced search may also be offered and requested. Such a search may utilize additional features and syntax, such as boolean and negation operators. Many such query languages exist, and no attempt is made to standardize any syntax in this document.
If advanced searches are supported by the server, it should include a text field in the MAM query form with the name {&ns;}fulltext and advertise a urn:xmpp:fulltext:0 feature via Service Discovery.

The <field/> element SHOULD contain a <desc/> element (as defined in &xep0004;) with a natural-language description of the search syntax. This element should possess an xml:lang attribute when appropriate.
Additionally, a <syntax/> element qualified by the &ns; namespace MAY be included, with the content being a value from the search syntax types registry defined later in this document.
Finally, as with the simple search field, a comma-separated list of supported languages MAY be provided in the <lang/> element, if the search functionality is optimized for specific languages.

example.caption: Server offers advanced text search functionality

section2.example: <iq type='result' id='form1'> <query xmlns='urn:xmpp:mam:2'> <x xmlns='jabber:x:data' type='form'> <field type='hidden' var='FORM_TYPE'> <value>urn:xmpp:mam:2</value> </field> <field type='jid-single' var='with'/> <field type='text-single' var='start'/> <field type='text-single' var='end'/> <field type='text-single' var='{urn:xmpp:fulltext:0}fulltext'> <desc xml:lang="en"> Enclose exact phrases in "double quotes", exclude search terms by prefixing with '-'. </desc> <syntax xmlns="urn:xmpp:fulltext:0" type="postgres-websearch"/> <lang xmlns="urn:xmpp:fulltext:0">en,fr</lang> </field> </x> </query> </iq>

section2.p: Support for this protocol can be discovered by requesting the MAM query form as described in XEP-0313, or via the Service Discovery protocol defined in &xep0030; using a feature of &ns;#simple if simple searches are supported, and/or &ns; if advanced searches are supported.

Searching using full text is performed by the client supplying an additional text key for either the &ns;#simple or &ns; fields described above. If either field is present in a query, the server MUST only include results which contain text matching the search query and match any other filtering criteria defined in the query. In the case that a server supports both search types, clients SHOULD NOT include both fields simultaneously in a query - the server behaviour upon receipt of a query containing both fields SHOULD result in an error.
Clients SHOULD ensure that xml:lang is set appropriately on the form submission, to allow the server to optimize results for the user's preferred language.

section1.code:
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?> <xs:schema xmlns:xs='http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema' targetNamespace='urn:xmpp:fulltext:0' xmlns='urn:xmpp:fulltext:0' elementFormDefault='qualified'>
<xs:annotation> <xs:documentation> The protocol documented by this schema is defined in XEP-0431: http://xmpp.org/extensions/xep-0431.html </xs:documentation> </xs:annotation>
<xs:element name='lang' type='xs:string'/>
<xs:element name='syntax'> <xs:complexType> <xs:attribute name='type' type='xs:string' use='required'/> </xs:complexType> </xs:element>
</xs:schema>

section1.p: The authors are not aware of any security issues raised by this specification.
This XEP requires no interaction with &IANA;.
This document defines a new registry of advanced search syntax types.

section2.section3:
The XMPP Registrar maintains a registry at &SEARCHSYNTAX; that defines values for the 'type' attribute of the <syntax/> element qualified by the '&ns;' namespace. ®PROCESS;
<syntax-type> <name> The (unique) name that identifies this syntax. </name> <description> A human-readable description of the syntax type. </description> <url> A URL where the syntax is described and documented. </url> </syntax-type>

section3.p: As part of this document, the following status codes are registered:
section3.code: <syntax-type> <name> lucene </name> <description> Apache Lucene default query parser syntax. </description> <url> https://lucene.apache.org/core/9_2_0/queryparser/org/apache/lucene/queryparser/flexible/standard/StandardQueryParser.html </url> </syntax-type> <syntax-type> <name> postgres-tsquery </name> <description> PostgreSQL 'tsquery' syntax </description> <url> https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/textsearch-controls.html#TEXTSEARCH-PARSING-QUERIES </url> </syntax-type> <syntax-type> <name> postgres-websearch </name> <description> PostgreSQL 'websearch' syntax </description> <url> https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/textsearch-controls.html#TEXTSEARCH-PARSING-QUERIES </url> </syntax-type> <syntax-type> <name> sqlite-fts5 </name> <description> SQLite 3.x FTS5 extension full text query syntax </description> <url> https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html </url> </syntax-type>
